title: Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: “Price is what you pay; value is what you get.”
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

book_paragraphs: Valuation is where a strong operating narrative meets the discipline of arithmetic. On the 2026-11-23 NSE market-facts ledger cutoff, TD Power Systems closed at ₹605.30. By the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, the share price had fallen further to ₹587.05, down 31.43% from its 52-week high of ₹856.10. At that live 2026-11-25 close, TradingView reports a market capitalization of ₹19,457.29 crore and a trailing P/E of 54.19x, while Screener's same-session fundamental card shows a market capitalization of ₹18,871 crore and a trailing P/E of 55.7x. That roughly 3% market-cap gap reflects vendor timing differences in incorporating the October 2026 equity raise rather than a disagreement on valuation posture. Either way, the market still values TDPS at roughly 54x to 56x trailing earnings and 14.09x book value [1][2][42].

This multiple compression from 71.1x on 12 November to 54.19x on 25 November did not happen because operations collapsed. On the contrary, the 13 November Q2 FY2027 earnings call delivered a material operational upgrade. Management lifted FY2027 revenue guidance from ₹2,600 crore to ₹2,900–₹3,000 crore, set initial FY2028 guidance at ₹3,400–₹3,500 crore, and held the 19 November ground-breaking for a dedicated fourth plant serving Siemens Energy [40][46]. Simultaneously, H1 FY2027 consolidated operating cash flow inflected sharply to ₹211.74 crore, roughly 101% of H1 consolidated net profit of ₹210.04 crore, versus just ₹12.60 crore a year earlier [42].

So why did the stock fall more than 6% in the week following a guidance upgrade and drop 19.60% over three months? The answer lies in what the market is now discounting beneath the headline revenue growth. First, direct and deemed exports surged to 90–92% of H1 FY2027 order inflows of ₹1,406 crore, exposing the company directly to cumulative 50% U.S. tariffs on Indian goods. Management's contingency plan to route partial assembly through its Turkey subsidiary for a 15% tariff nameplate introduces customs scrutiny, rules-of-origin risk, and dual-site logistics friction [44]. Second, standalone trade receivables jumped 35% in six months from ₹708.65 crore in March 2026 to ₹956.31 crore in September 2026, showing that working capital still absorbs cash as scale grows [42].

Third, capital allocation and ownership signals have turned noisier. TDPS raised ₹675 crore in fresh equity via a ₹75 crore promoter preferential allotment at ₹600 per share and a ₹600 crore QIP at ₹775 per share, yet the 12 November interim filing offered no itemized proceeds-deployment schedule [42]. Promoter shareholding stepped down from 34.27% in September 2024 to 26.87% in June 2025 following a ₹530 crore open-market sale, and now sits at 26.51% post-QIP with nil pledges. Meanwhile, institutional holder Oxbow Capital Management cut its stake in half from 3.08% to 1.42% via open-market sales through 13 November 2026 [45]. When insiders monetize at highs, a QIP expands the share count, and an institutional holder exits into a guidance raise, multiple compression is a rational market response.

A clean reverse-DCF exercise strips away the narrative and reveals what the ₹18,871–₹19,457 crore valuation still demands. Because TDPS is virtually debt-free (debt-to-equity of 0.00x) and held ₹288.89 crore of consolidated cash before October QIP proceeds, equity market capitalization serves as a reasonable baseline proxy for operating value, though audited post-QIP net cash and lease liabilities will refine enterprise value in the FY2027 annual report [1][42]. Using TradingView's ₹19,457 crore market cap, a steady-state 40x industrial multiple requires ₹486 crore of annual net profit. A more conventional 35x multiple requires ₹556 crore, and a 30x cyclical capital-goods multiple requires ₹649 crore.

Compare those earnings hurdles against the company's actual trajectory. Audited FY2026 consolidated revenue was ₹1,856 crore, operating profit ₹335 crore (18.05% margin), and net profit ₹239 crore [1]. Implied trailing twelve-month net profit sits near ₹339–₹359 crore (derived from Screener's ₹18,871 crore at 55.7x and TradingView's ₹19,457 crore at 54.19x). If TDPS hits the midpoint of its upgraded FY2027 revenue guidance at ₹2,950 crore and holds a 19% EBITDA margin, operating profit reaches roughly ₹560 crore and net profit approaches ₹395–₹415 crore. If FY2028 hits ₹3,450 crore at an 18.5%–19.0% EBITDA margin—accounting for management's flagged temporary dip during fourth-plant ramp-up—net profit can reach ₹455–₹495 crore [40][46].

That bridge exposes the core valuation tension. Even if TDPS executes its upgraded FY2028 guidance flawlessly, a ₹480 crore net profit at 40x earnings produces a ₹19,200 crore market capitalization—essentially flat with today's ₹19,457 crore valuation. In other words, at ₹587.05 per share, the market is already pricing in full delivery of FY2027 and FY2028 guidance at a premium 40x multiple. To earn a meaningful positive return from here over two years, investors must bet on one of two outcomes: either earnings beat the ₹3,500 crore FY2028 target by a wide margin, or the market continues to award a 45x–50x multiple despite tariff risk, single-OEM build-to-print concentration, and cyclical capital-goods history.

Per-share dilution sharpens that test. Before the recent equity raises, TDPS had roughly 31.2 crore shares outstanding. Adding the ₹600 crore QIP at ₹775 per share (roughly 0.77 crore shares) and the ₹75 crore promoter preferential allotment at ₹600 per share (0.125 crore shares) lifts the diluted share base toward 32.1–33.1 crore shares, consistent with Screener's ₹18,871 crore and TradingView's ₹19,457 crore market capitalizations at ₹587.05 [42]. On a 32.5 crore diluted share base, ₹405 crore of FY2027 net profit yields roughly ₹12.45 in diluted EPS, while ₹480 crore of FY2028 net profit yields roughly ₹14.75. To reconcile the two-year bridge explicitly: FY2028E midpoint profit of ₹480 crore on 32.5 crore shares equals ₹14.75 diluted EPS, so our ₹16.00 Base Case diluted EPS (₹520 crore PAT) is an explicit FY2029E estimate representing an 8.5% step-up beyond FY2028E guidance and 45% to 53% cumulative profit growth from current TTM levels.

Cash-flow forensics reinforce the case for valuation discipline. In FY2026, consolidated operating cash flow was just ₹129 crore against ₹239 crore of net profit (54% conversion) and ₹105 crore of investing cash outflows, leaving minimal free cash flow [1]. The H1 FY2027 rebound to ₹211.74 crore of CFO (~101% of H1 PAT) is a genuine step forward and proves the business can collect cash when milestone payments align [42]. However, one strong half-year does not erase a ten-year record of lumpy cash conversion, especially when standalone trade receivables rose 35% in the same six months to ₹956.31 crore and management is breaking ground on a capital-intensive fourth plant for Siemens Energy without disclosing binding purchase-order minimums [42][46].

Peer comparison provides a sobering external check. No listed Indian company is a pure-play twin for TDPS's custom AC generator mix, so peers act as valuation guardrails rather than exact pricing formulas. On the 2026-11-25 TradingView snapshot, Cummins India trades at ₹4,067.00 (₹1,13,153 crore market cap) on 50.06x TTM P/E with 17.13% operating margins and 27.81% ROE, while sitting in a deep Stage 4 markdown (-33.33% off its 52-week high) as TTM revenue growth slowed to 9.87% and EPS dipped 2.69%. CG Power trades at ₹778.90 (₹1,23,928 crore market cap) on 89.26x P/E with 11.59% operating margins and 23.76% revenue growth, also locked in Stage 4 (-20.59% off its high). ABB India trades at ₹7,028.50 (₹1,45,412 crore market cap) on 49.30x P/E with 13.21% operating margins and 7.90% revenue growth, basing in Stage 1.

Notice the sector-wide message in that peer table. TDPS clearly outpaces Cummins India, CG Power, and ABB India on TTM revenue growth (+65.03%), EPS growth (+62.51%), operating margin (17.74%), and ROCE (34.0% on Screener). That operating superiority explains why the market still pays 54.2x–55.7x for TDPS even after a 31% stock drawdown. Yet Cummins India and CG Power are both in Stage 4 markdowns right alongside TDPS. When larger, better-diversified electrical-equipment peers with deeper aftermarket service franchises are compressing to 49x–50x earnings during a sector rotation, a smaller single-product generator supplier with 90–92% export exposure and U.S. tariff friction cannot rely on multiple expansion to bail out an expensive entry.

To make valuation actionable rather than academic, we build three explicit two-year (FY2028–FY2029) scenarios on the post-QIP diluted share base. Our Bear case (35% probability) values TDPS at ₹410 per share, assuming ₹11.70 diluted EPS at a 35x multiple. This occurs if U.S. tariff routing through Turkey stalls shipments, data-centre gas-turbine orders normalize after an initial wave, receivables stretch further, and the market re-rates TDPS toward a standard cyclical industrial multiple. At live CMP ₹587.05, our 35x Bear case represents 30.2% downside. Under a harsher 30x cyclical capital-goods stress multiple, even flawless FY2028E midpoint delivery (₹14.75 EPS × 30x) values the stock at ₹442.50 (-24.6% from ₹587.05), while Bear earnings (₹11.70 EPS × 30x) drop fair value to ₹351.00 (-40.2%).

Our Base case (45% probability) values TDPS at ₹720 per share, trimmed from the prior dossier's ₹820 to reflect post-QIP share dilution, build-to-print single-OEM IP dependency, and ongoing U.S. tariff/receivables friction. It models explicit FY2029E diluted EPS of ₹16.00 (~₹520 crore PAT on 32.5 crore shares, stepping up +8.5% from FY2028E midpoint ₹14.75 EPS as FY2028 ₹3,400–₹3,500 crore guidance converts at 18.5%–19.0% EBITDA margins) valued at 45x earnings rather than 50x. From live CMP ₹587.05, the Base case implies +22.6% two-year upside—respectable in isolation, but insufficient to compensate for 30.2% bear-case downside while the stock is in a broken Stage 4 downtrend.

Our Bull case (20% probability) values TDPS at ₹990 per share, assuming diluted EPS reaches ₹19.80 at a 50x multiple. That requires a clean resolution of U.S. tariff friction without margin leakage, smooth ramp-up of the Siemens Energy 125–325 MW two-pole generator plant ahead of Q1 CY2028, sustained 19%–20% EBITDA margins, and disciplined working capital where CFO consistently tracks 90%–100% of PAT [40][42][46]. Weighting these three outcomes produces a probability-weighted two-year fair value of ₹665.50 (roughly ₹666), which is only +13.4% above the live 2026-11-25 close of ₹587.05.

The valuation verdict is therefore straightforward. TD Power Systems is no longer absurdly priced at 71x earnings, and its upgraded FY2027–FY2028 revenue trajectory gives fundamental support over a multi-year window. However, at 54x–56x trailing earnings against a probability-weighted fair value of ₹666 and a bear-case floor of ₹410, the valuation offers no margin of safety to fight a Stage 4 downtrend. New capital is rejected on both trend and valuation grounds until price either resets to a far deeper discount or earnings growth catches up while the chart rebuilds a confirmed Stage 1 base and Stage 2 breakout.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a stock drops 31% from its high and still trades at 55 times earnings, the market is telling you two things at once: the business is growing fast, and the starting expectations were even faster. Never confuse a falling multiple with a cheap stock until you test what steady-state earnings must be at 35x to 40x.
